title: Mean time to fixation of a neutral mutant

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mean time to fixation of a neutral mutant

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A neutral mutant that does go to fixation takes on average about four times the effective population size, in generations, to do so.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population (1969)

fields.label: Source as written
fields.value: Motoo Kimura (1969) The average number of generations until fixation of a mutant gene in a finite population

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: Cursor agent (Claude Opus 5.5) extracting key claims from source papers

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, neutrality, constant N_e

fields.label: Formal status in the nanopub
fields.value: proved within the diffusion limit (Kimura and Ohta 1969).

fields.label: Proposed test
fields.value: In replicate small populations of known N_e, record the conditional time to fixation of neutral marker alleles and compare it with 4N_e generations.
